hero.title: Project Pyramid
hero.sub: A stealth-adventure set in ancient Egypt, featuring a modular AI architecture and advanced sensory systems.
hero.img_alt: Unreal Engine C++ AI System Architecture Diagram: interaction between Base AI Controller, Dual-Cone Perception (Direct and Peripheral Sight), World Subsystem, and Pooled Deception Dummy Entity.
hero.img1_alt: Logical flowchart of the Dummy Manager Subsystem in Unreal Engine C++: Object Pooling lifecycle, Active Viewers tracking, and AI Deception trigger conditions
img1_desc: Implementation of a UWorldSubsystem managing a decoy actor ADummyEntity
to deceive AI perception when the player breaks line of sight.
To eliminate runtime spawn overhead and garbage collection spikes, the subsystem utilizes an Object Pooling pattern
instantiating a single actor on level initialization and relocating it on demand.
An active viewer counter ActiveViewersCount ensures the dummy only activates when all enemies completely lose visual contact,
paired with an automatic threshold distance check to invalidate the decoy if the player moves too far
hero.img2_alt: Unreal Engine C++ code snippet: UDummyManagerSubsystem (UWorldSubsystem) and ADummyEntity interface declarations showing IGenericTeamAgentInterface and AI Perception stimuli integration
img2_desc: Declaration of the C++ classes for managing the Dummy. ADummyEntity extends AActor and inherits from IGenericTeamAgentInterface,
overriding GetGenericTeamId() with the same identifier as the player; this ensures that the AI treats the decoy as a legitimate hostile target.
The UAIPerceptionStimuliSourceComponent emits the visual stimulus required for the deception.

On the management side, UDummyManagerSubsystem inherits from UWorldSubsystem, ensuring its lifecycle is tied to the game world without the need for singleton constructs or dummy actors placed within the scene.
hero.img3_alt: Unreal Engine C++ code snippet: custom AI Sight senses (Direct and Peripheral Sight) and custom Environment Query System (EQS) test driven by Data Tables
img3_desc: Out of the box, Unreal Engine's AI Perception operates with a single uniform sight cone.
To support nuanced stealth and alertness mechanics, I extended the perception pipeline by creating two independent senses: Direct Sight (narrow cone, fast detection)
and Peripheral Sight (wide field of view, progressive detection timer based on distance).
To empower tactical navigation and cover evaluation (e.g.: cover or stroll outside the target sight),
I authored a custom Environment Query System test UEqt_IsPointInVision extending UEnvQueryTest.
It filters environmental query points against the active vision cones at runtime, fully driven by designer-friendly Data Tables FPerceptionsParam.

text: Project Pyramid is an ongoing collaborative team project.
My role as AI Systems Programmer is currently concluded/paused after delivering the core enemy architecture and perception framework.
The team is now proceeding with level design, asset creation, and puzzle mechanics.

concept.title: Stealth AI Engineering
desc: In a stealth-focused experience, the AI is the heart of the gameplay loop. I was responsible for designing a system that wasn't just 'reactive', but believable.

From managing enemy memory via the Dummy System to reinforcement coordination, the goal was to create a scalable framework that designers could easily tune via Data Tables without touching the codebase.

points.1: Dummy Entity World Subsystem: Implemented a C++ system that spawns a 'ghost' entity at the player's last known position. AI units investigate the Dummy instead of 'cheating' with omniscience, creating realistic search patterns.
points.2: Multi-State AI (C++/BT): Developed a modular Behavior Tree architecture with 5 primary states (Patrol, Alert, Search, Combat, Dead). It features dynamic perception management that live-updates sensory parameters based on the current state.
points.3: Coordination & Roles: Implemented a synchronized 'Call for Aid' system to prevent overlapping enemy yells. Added role assignment logic (Investigator vs. Support) to ensure enemies surround the player during investigations.
points.4: EQS & Flanking: Leveraged the Environment Query System for dynamic flanking in combat and to claim exclusive search points, preventing multiple AI agents from stacking on the same spot.
points.5: Slide Component: Built a standalone, slope-aware sliding mechanic for the player character using vector projection and VLerp of terrain normals for smooth traversal.

lessons.title: Workflow & Tooling
desc: I focused on system optimization by migrating Tick-based components (like footstep detection) to high-performance Anim Notifies.

To improve team iteration, I created editor tools via Construction Scripts to visualize patrol paths, indices, and wait times directly in the viewport, removing the need to check individual array elements.

points.3: Dynamic Flanking and Point Claiming via EQS
points.4: Data Table-driven AI for rapid balancing
points.6: Custom Editor Tooling for Spline Patrols
